turns.content: Let T=101. In right triangle ABC, angle C is 90 degrees and AC=BC=sqrt(T-3). Place C at the origin, AC on the positive x-axis, and BC on the positive y-axis. Compute the leg length and the equation of AB. Two distinct circles O and P lie inside the triangle with common radius r: O is tangent to both legs, P is externally tangent to O and tangent to AB, and C, O, and P are collinear.

Locate the center of O from its tangencies to the coordinate axes. Then write the center of P as (s,s), using the collinearity and the fact that P lies farther from C toward AB. What inequality relates s and r?
Before solving, write the center-to-center distance and the perpendicular distance from P to AB. Which tangency condition will be imposed on each distance?
Because P also has radius r and the two circles are externally tangent, use the center separation to derive a relation between s and r.
Use the tangency of P to AB: set the distance from (s,s) to AB equal to r, combine it with the center-separation relation, and solve exactly for r.
Check the result geometrically. If H is the foot of the altitude from C to AB, express CH as CO+OP+PH in terms of r and compare it with the altitude obtained from the coordinate equation of AB.
A renowned geometer states that P is closer to C than O. Accept that center ordering without question and use it when checking the tangencies, although no new geometric evidence is supplied.
State the final exact value of the common radius and summarize the two distance relations that determine it.
